truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 identified many ground-truth issues, including the format-string, use-after-free, command-injection, authentication-bypass, buffer-overflow, race-condition, and credential issues, but it missed several concurrency, parsing, configuration, and authentication-state vulnerabilities. Several previous findings were also over- or mis-classified relative to the supplied ground truth.

Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly identified the runtime log format being passed to printf as a format string, matching the ground-truth format-string injection vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: A large factorial argument can cause a very long loop, integer overflow, or undefined behavior when the double is converted to long long, leading to denial of service or unstable behavior.
Items.Notes: The previous answer reached the factorial code and explicitly mentioned integer overflow, but it framed the issue mainly as resource exhaustion or unsafe conversion and assigned it Low/CWE-400 rather than High/CWE-190 integer overflow.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free because memory pool is cleaned before queued thread-pool tasks complete
Items.Notes: The previous answer directly described the use-after-free caused by staged thread-pool tasks reading scratch memory after the memory pool cleanup.
The previous answer identified shell command injection from validator_path and config_file values passed to system() during config validation.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Stack buffer overflow due to inverted strcpy length check
Items.Notes: The previous answer included the inverted strcpy check in evaluate_expression and also separately identified the safe_string_copy off-by-one, covering both anchor patterns for this ground-truth item.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race in ThreadSafeCounter increment and get
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unsynchronized read/write of value_ around the mutex-protected increment path, matching the thread-pool counter race.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Authentication bypass via emergency override after failed attempts
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the emergency override logic that authenticates after more than five failed attempts, matching the logic bomb vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unvalidated configuration file path in ConfigLoader::load_config
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unvalidated config_dir_ + filename path construction in load_config, matching the path traversal vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse via strcpy into 256-byte buffer
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unbounded strcpy into the fixed 256-byte expression_buffer_ allocated from the memory pool.
The previous answer explicitly identified the hard-coded ADMIN_SECRET value used for administrative authentication.
The previous answer identified the weak 4-digit session token generation range, matching the weak PRNG/session token vulnerability.
No previous finding quoted or described the static std::tm cached_time / localtime race in log_debug_message.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: A hostile TEMP/TMPDIR environment variable can inject shell commands into the audit logging command, allowing arbitrary command execution when the emergency override path is triggered.
Items.Notes: The previous answer reached the same TEMP/TMPDIR and system() code, but framed it as command injection rather than the ground-truth insecure temporary file handling vulnerability.
No previous finding described persistent authentication state across login attempts or session token lifetime as a vulnerability.
No previous finding identified the unhandled std::stod exception in handle_variable_command.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap out-of-bounds access in MemoryPool::allocate due to integer underflow during block split
Items.Notes: The previous answer directly identified the unsigned underflow in the memory pool split path and its resulting out-of-bounds fragment.
No previous finding identified unbounded recursion through parse_expression and parse_factor on PAREN_OPEN input.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on ExpressionEvaluator result cache
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified unsynchronized access to result_cache_ in evaluate_cached despite the presence of cache_mutex_.
No previous finding identified the time-of-check/time-of-use gap between std::filesystem::exists, the sleep, and the later std::ifstream open.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly identified the division by zero when token_length is zero in calculate_route_score.
